patch_description: The SLSQP polish maximizes the non-smooth dmin and often stalls because its gradient only sees the single bottleneck pair. Following the recommendation, I add a cheap micro-search stage applied to the top-2 candidates: identify the point involved in the smallest pairwise distance, nudge it a small step along the direction away from its nearest neighbor (i.e., along the gradient of that pair's distance), then re-run one short SLSQP pass. This directly attacks the binding constraint without disturbing the overall configuration. Since dmin/dmax for 14 points in 3D is bounded by a kissing-number style argument, small targeted escapes from stalled minima are exactly where gains remain.
